Measured: `hasStateArtifacts` and `hasRecordedRoundFiles` have exactly ONE caller between them — `LoadReviewState` at `internal/engine/reviewstate.go:130` and `:136` (searched `internal/` for both names; the only other hits are their own definitions and two test files). Neither reaches phase detection. So the mutant's real consequence is not a different phase: on the ground-only directory §7.3 itself mandates — "holding only the ground round and its snapshot, with no `state.json`" — `LoadReviewState` takes the `os.IsNotExist` branch, finds `hasStateArtifacts` true, and returns `StateCorruptError{MissingIndex: true}`. Every command that loads state for that spec ABORTS. The conclusion (keep ground out of both lists) survives intact and is if anything better supported; the stated mechanism does not, and row 11 inherits it verbatim ("makes a ground-only spec read as having review state and changes the phase the oracle reports"). This document defines a verdict for exactly this — PARTIAL / `reason-not-conclusion` — and §7.3 is an instance of it.
suggestion: Falsifier: a caller of `hasStateArtifacts` or `hasRecordedRoundFiles` inside the phase oracle — searched, there is none. Restate the reason as the corrupt-state abort, and strengthen row 11 with it: assert `LoadReviewState` returns `(nil, nil)` on a directory holding only `ground-round-1.ndjson` and `snapshot-ground-round-1.md`. That is a bounded read-back of a returned value rather than a comparison of a phase string, so it fails on the mutant for the reason the row states, and it is the assertion shape this project has recorded as the one a rewording cannot slip past.

finding: "A unit whose `text_sha` matches a disposition in the previous round carries it forward" does not say where the carried disposition lives, and the three answers produce three different artifacts and three different coverage numbers. (a) The unit re-records it — then a second pass is not scoped and §8's argument for `text_sha` ("twelve full passes where the design intends one and eleven scoped ones") is lost. (b) tp materialises it into `ground-round-N.ndjson` at record — then the round file holds rows no unit wrote, and §7.2's "one JSON object per line" schema has no field distinguishing them. (c) tp joins across rounds at `--status` time — then `ground-round-N.ndjson` is not self-describing and §7.1's `--status --check` ("every emitted floor unit carries a disposition") is a claim about a set of files rather than about a round. §11 row 16 asserts the join predicate and is satisfied by all three. A second question rides on it: "the previous round" — round N-1 only, or transitively the most recent round holding that `text_sha`? Under N-1 only, a unit carried through round 2 and untouched in round 3 becomes uncovered again for no reason.
suggestion: Name the locus in one sentence and say whether the lookup is transitive: e.g. "tp materialises the carried row into round N at record with `carried_from: <N>`, and the lookup walks back to the most recent round holding that `text_sha`". Add the field to §7.2 if it exists, and extend row 16's mutant to the chain case (a unit carried across two rounds).

finding: The carry-forward joins on text_sha alone while §7.2 puts an anchor on every row that the join does not use. Two identical sentences in different sections share a hash — this repository ships a duplicate-paragraph lint rule because that happens in specs — so a unit deleted from one section can inherit a disposition earned by an identical sentence elsewhere, and a unit whose section was rewritten around it keeps its verdict. Row 16 can be built either way and passes either way, so the row does not pin the rule.
suggestion: State the join key as the pair (anchor, text_sha) if section identity matters, or state that text_sha alone is deliberate and duplicate sentences share one disposition by design; name the choice in row 16 so its fixture is determined. Falsifier: a guarantee that no two floor units in a spec share a text_sha — no spec has that property and §2.1 does not give it one.

finding: The release's stated purpose is that `tp ground` "makes the premises verified rather than asserted" (§1.2), and nothing it emits can tell a verified spec from a refuted one. §7.1: `--status --check` "exits 0 when every emitted floor unit carries a disposition". §8: coverage is dispositions over the emitted floor, and FAIL is a disposition. §8's carry-forward then makes it permanent: an UNREPAIRED FAIL keeps its text, so its `text_sha` matches on the next pass, its disposition carries forward, and the unit stays covered without anyone touching it. A spec with forty-four recorded FAILs therefore exits 0 on `--check` in round 1 and in every round after, and §9's advisory does not close the gap either — it fires only "when any unit is undispositioned or when no ground round exists", so the operator's one-bit signal reads identically for a fully-verified spec and a fully-refuted one. §11 row 15 pins the denominator and numerator and no row reads a verdict. Non-Goal 3 forbids REFUSING on coverage; it does not forbid REPORTING the mix, and §9's own precedent argues for it — "`divergence` reported for a release before anything gated on it".
suggestion: Falsifier: any field §7.1 or §9 says `--status` carries beyond coverage — both say only coverage, so there is none. Add one sentence to §7.1 or §8 stating that `--status` reports a per-verdict breakdown of the latest round beside the coverage ratio, and that `--check`'s exit code is unaffected by it (which keeps Non-Goal 3 intact and keeps §7.1's one-bit read-back one bit). Add a row asserting the breakdown is present and that a round of all-FAIL rows still exits 0 on `--check` — which pins the deliberate separation rather than leaving a reader to discover it.

finding: 'Five role prompts times twelve rounds is sixty emissions' names a panel size that does not exist here. Measured: /tmp/tp-dev/tp review spec/1.0.0.md emits four prompts (architect, ax-economist, implementer, tester), .tp/reviewers/ holds those four files, and the embedded default software corpus (internal/engine/corpus/software/reviewers/) holds three. Four times twelve is forty-eight. Row 17 repeats the figure as the mutant's cost, so the one §11 row over §9 quotes it too. The arithmetic is internally consistent, which is what makes it survive reading — it is §5's own class, a borrowed number in a sentence that was cheap to write, inside the release whose subject is that class.
suggestion: Say four times twelve, or drop the multiplication and state the shape instead ('once per role per round rather than once per round'), which no corpus change falsifies. Falsifier: a reviewer corpus in this repository or in the embedded defaults holding five review roles — neither does, on the commands above.

finding: The repair strengthened a claim while deleting its anchor. Baseline §1: the four escapes recorded in `scripts/check-measured-claims.py`'s header "each one is a constraint **on §2 and §7**". New §1: "each is a constraint **this spec adopts**" — a stronger assertion (adopted, not merely binding) with no section named and no §11 row implementing any of the four. Checked against the new text: (i) "a claim reworded past its pattern must still fail" — §8 joins on `text_sha`, so a reworded claim loses its carry-forward and is re-decided, which is arguably adoption; (ii) "the derivation rule is read from the document rather than held in the checker" — nothing; §2.1's arms are held in tp; (iii) "a claimed list compares as a set, because cardinality alone passed a body of 100 fabricated entries" — nothing; §8's coverage is a count, and row 15's only set-like guard is that `unit_id: null` rows are excluded; (iv) "a placeholder beside real entries is a contradiction rather than an exemption" — nothing. The same paragraph also drops "it is what found the 49 unresolvable citations in the pending set", the one measured result showing the precedent is live rather than merely registered.
suggestion: Either name where each constraint lands (i → §8's `text_sha` join; ii/iii/iv → state which are deliberately not adopted by this release and why), or revert to the baseline's weaker and accurate "each is a constraint on §2 and §7". Restore the 49-citation result, which is the evidence that the precedent is exercised.

finding: The repair keeps the record of the withdrawn floor figures — correctly, since the baseline's own §2 established that a withdrawal must be visible — but misquotes the figure it is withdrawing, and drops the datum the withdrawal rested on. §2.1: "Two earlier drafts quoted one — *'15 of 46 sentences'*, then *'73 of 55'*". The second draft is the round-1 baseline, `spec/.tp-review/1.0.0/snapshot-round-1.md:108-111`, whose table reads `| this file | 73 | 55 | **75%** |` under the headers `prose units | caught by the floor | share` — that is **55 of 73**, not "73 of 55", which is a ratio above 1 and reads as a third figure nobody ever quoted. The baseline also carried "The closest is 21 of 55", the one reproducible number the withdrawal of "15 of 46" was grounded on; the repair drops it, leaving the withdrawal asserted rather than evidenced. Since §2.1's whole argument is that unreproducible figures are the defect, misreporting the figure being retired is the argument failing on itself.
suggestion: Write "*'15 of 46 sentences'*, then *'55 of 73 prose units'*", and keep "sixteen readings of the counting rule came no closer than 21 of 55" — it is the measurement that makes the withdrawal a finding rather than a preference.

finding: §3's `PASS` row cites the wrong subsection for the concept the whole record contract turns on: "evidence at or above the claim's minimum tier (**§4.2**) supports it". §4.2 is "Where the probe runs"; the `kind` → minimum-`tier` table is in **§4.1**. The error is a direct product of this repair's own restructuring — the baseline's §4.1 was "Where the probe runs", and the repair inserted a new §4.1 ("Kinds and tiers") that pushed it to §4.2 — so a reference written against the old numbering points at the old slot. §3's `FAIL` row says "at or above the minimum tier" with no citation at all, so the enum table an implementer must find is named once and named wrongly. `tp lint`'s `broken-cross-ref` rule cannot catch this: it fires only on the `§X.Y step N` form.
suggestion: Change the `PASS` row's citation to §4.1 and add the same citation to the `FAIL` row.

finding: §4.2 calls the ground clause "a third constant beside the two v0.36.0 §2.2 defines". `internal/cli/clauses.go` records the split differently in three places: its file comment at `:5` reads "The two clauses v0.36.0 §2 **and §3** append to every emitted role prompt", `:17-18` names `isolationClause` as "§2.2", and `:21` names `incrementalClause` as "§3.2". `spec/0.36.0.md`'s headings agree — §2.2 is "The clause" (singular) and §2.3 is "Placement, to the byte". So §2.2 defines ONE constant, not two. The clause count itself is right (there are two today and ground makes three); only the attribution is wrong. It matters slightly more than a typo because §4.2's next sentence draws a scope line against "v0.36.0 §6.2's byte-for-byte suffix assertion", and a reader following the §2.2 pointer to find the second constant lands in the wrong section for it.
suggestion: Falsifier: a second constant defined in `spec/0.36.0.md` §2.2 — its heading is "The clause", singular, and `clauses.go:21` attributes the other to §3.2. Reword to "a third constant beside the two v0.36.0 §2.2 and §3.2 define", matching `clauses.go:5`.
